stem: All matter is made up of tiny __________ that are too small to be seen.
solution: Matter is composed of extremely small particles.

stem: The three common states of matter are __________.
solution: Matter commonly exists as solid, liquid and gas.

stem: In a solid, the particles are __________.
options: very closely packed and fixed in position
solution: Solid particles are tightly packed in fixed positions, giving solids a definite shape and volume.

stem: A solid has a __________ shape and a __________ volume.
solution: Solids have both a definite shape and a definite volume.

stem: In a liquid, the particles are __________ than in a solid.
options: slightly farther apart and can move around
solution: Liquid particles are a little farther apart and can slide past one another, so liquids flow.

stem: A liquid has a definite __________ but takes the shape of its container.
solution: Liquids have a fixed volume but no fixed shape; they take the container's shape.

stem: In a gas, the particles are __________.
options: very far apart and move freely and fast
solution: Gas particles are widely separated and move rapidly and randomly, filling any container.

stem: A gas has __________ shape and __________ volume.
solution: A gas has neither a definite shape nor a definite volume; it fills its container.

stem: Gases can be compressed easily because their particles __________.
solution: The large gaps between gas particles allow gases to be compressed.

stem: Solids and liquids are difficult to compress because their particles are __________.
solution: In solids and liquids the particles are already close, leaving little space to compress.

stem: The spreading of a smell across a room shows that particles of matter __________.
solution: The smell spreads because particles move and mix with the air — evidence of particle motion.

stem: The intermixing of particles of two substances on their own is called __________.
solution: Diffusion is the spontaneous mixing of particles due to their constant motion.

stem: Diffusion is fastest in __________.
options: it is the same in all
solution: Because gas particles move fastest and are farthest apart, diffusion is quickest in gases.

stem: When a crystal of potassium permanganate is dropped in water, the colour spreads through the water, showing __________.
solution: The colour spreads by diffusion, as the particles move and mix through the water.

stem: The particles of matter are held together by forces of __________.
solution: Forces of attraction between particles hold matter together.

stem: The force of attraction between particles is strongest in __________.
solution: Solids have the strongest interparticle forces, keeping particles fixed.

stem: The force of attraction between particles is weakest in __________.
solution: Gases have the weakest forces between particles, so their particles move freely.

stem: The change of a solid directly into a liquid on heating is called __________.
solution: Melting is the change from solid to liquid on heating.

stem: The change of a liquid into a solid on cooling is called __________.
solution: Freezing is the change from liquid to solid on cooling.

stem: The change of a liquid into a gas is called __________.
solution: The change from liquid to gas is called evaporation (or boiling at the boiling point).

stem: The change of a gas into a liquid on cooling is called __________.
solution: Condensation is the change from gas to liquid on cooling.

stem: Some solids, like camphor, change directly into vapour on heating without becoming liquid; this is called __________.
solution: Sublimation is the direct change of a solid to gas (and vice versa) without a liquid stage.

stem: When matter changes from one state to another, the __________ of the particles changes but the particles remain the same.
solution: In a change of state, only the arrangement and motion of particles change; the substance is the same.

stem: Heating a substance generally makes its particles move __________.
solution: Heat increases the kinetic energy of particles, so they move faster.

stem: Cooling a substance generally makes its particles move __________.
solution: Cooling reduces particle energy, so they move more slowly and may come closer together.

stem: The temperature at which a solid melts is called its __________.
solution: The melting point is the temperature at which a solid turns to liquid.

stem: The temperature at which a liquid boils is called its __________.
solution: The boiling point is the temperature at which a liquid rapidly turns to gas.

stem: The melting point of ice at normal pressure is __________.
solution: Ice melts at 0 °C under normal atmospheric pressure.

stem: The boiling point of water at normal pressure is __________.
solution: Water boils at 100 °C under normal atmospheric pressure.

stem: Wet clothes dry even without boiling because of __________.
solution: Evaporation occurs at all temperatures from the surface of a liquid, drying wet clothes.

stem: Evaporation causes __________.
solution: Evaporation absorbs heat from the surroundings, producing a cooling effect.

stem: Water kept in an earthen pot (matka) stays cool because of __________.
options: evaporation of water through its pores
solution: Water seeping through the pores evaporates, taking heat and cooling the water inside.

stem: The rate of evaporation increases when the __________ increases.
solution: Higher temperature and larger exposed surface increase the rate of evaporation.

stem: Evaporation is slower when the surrounding air has high __________.
solution: High humidity means the air already holds much water vapour, slowing evaporation.

stem: The particles that make up matter have empty __________ between them.
solution: There are empty spaces between the particles of matter.

stem: Sugar dissolving in water and 'disappearing' shows that particles __________.
options: have spaces into which sugar particles fit
solution: The sugar particles occupy the spaces between the water particles, so the volume hardly changes.

stem: Which state of matter has the highest kinetic energy of particles at a given temperature?
solution: Gas particles move fastest and thus have the highest kinetic energy.

stem: Which of the following can flow?
solution: Both liquids and gases can flow and are together called fluids.

stem: Liquids and gases are together called __________.
solution: Fluids are substances that can flow — liquids and gases.

stem: A gas exerts pressure on the walls of its container because its particles __________.
solution: Fast-moving gas particles constantly strike the container walls, exerting pressure.

stem: Steam causes more severe burns than boiling water because steam contains extra __________.
solution: Steam releases additional heat as it condenses on the skin, causing worse burns.

stem: When water is heated, the change from ice to water to steam involves __________ of the particles.
solution: As water is heated, particles gain energy, move more and spread apart from solid to liquid to gas.

stem: The dew seen on grass in the early morning is formed by __________.
solution: Water vapour in the air condenses on cool surfaces at night, forming dew.

stem: Naphthalene balls slowly disappear over time because of __________.
solution: Naphthalene sublimes, changing directly from solid to vapour, so the balls shrink over time.

stem: The volume occupied by a fixed mass of gas __________ when it is compressed.
solution: Compressing a gas pushes its particles closer, reducing its volume.

stem: Which of the following best shows that gases have mass?
options: An inflated balloon weighs more than a deflated one
solution: The inflated balloon is heavier, showing the enclosed gas has mass.

stem: The main idea of the particulate nature of matter is that matter is __________.
options: made of moving particles with spaces between them
solution: Matter is made of tiny moving particles with spaces between them and forces of attraction.

stem: When a gas is cooled enough, it may change into a liquid; this is used to __________.
options: store gases like LPG in liquid form
solution: Cooling and compressing gases turns them to liquid, as with LPG stored in cylinders.

stem: A block of ice and liquid water are the same substance because both are made of __________.
solution: Ice and water are the same substance in different states, made of the same water particles.

stem: When a balloon is inflated, the gas inside spreads out to fill it because gas particles __________.
options: move freely and fill all the available space
solution: Gas particles move freely and spread to occupy the whole container, filling the balloon.

stem: Everything around us that has mass and occupies space is called:
solution: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space (has volume); everything around us — solids, liquids and gases — is made of matter.

stem: Matter is made up of tiny particles that are too small to be seen; this is the ______ nature of matter.
solution: The particulate nature of matter is the idea that all matter is made up of extremely tiny particles (atoms and molecules) that cannot be seen with the naked eye.

stem: The three states of matter are solid, liquid and:
solution: The three common states of matter are solid, liquid and gas; they differ in the arrangement and movement of their particles.

stem: In a solid, the particles are:
options: Far apart and free to move
Closely packed in a fixed arrangement, vibrating in place
solution: In solids, the particles are closely packed in a regular, fixed arrangement with strong forces between them; they can only vibrate about fixed positions, giving solids a definite shape and volume.

stem: In a gas, the particles are:
options: Far apart and move about freely and randomly
solution: In gases, the particles are far apart and move about freely and randomly at high speed, with very weak forces between them; gases have no fixed shape or volume.

stem: Which state of matter has a definite volume but takes the shape of its container?
solution: A liquid has a definite volume but no definite shape — it takes the shape of the container it is poured into, because its particles can move around but stay close together.

stem: The process by which particles of matter intermix on their own is called:
solution: Diffusion is the process by which the particles of two substances mix with each other on their own due to their constant random movement — e.g. the smell of perfume spreading in a room.

stem: Diffusion is fastest in ______ because their particles move most freely.
solution: Diffusion is fastest in gases because their particles are far apart and move very fast and freely; it is slower in liquids and slowest (almost negligible) in solids.

stem: The fact that we can smell food cooking from a distance is evidence of:
options: The particulate nature of matter (particles diffusing through air)
solution: Smelling food from a distance shows that tiny particles of matter (from the food) diffuse through the air and reach our nose — evidence of the particulate nature of matter and diffusion.

stem: When sugar dissolves in water and disappears from view, but the water tastes sweet, it shows that:
options: Matter is made of tiny particles that spread among the water particles
solution: When sugar dissolves, its tiny particles spread out and fit into the spaces between the water particles, so it becomes invisible but the water tastes sweet — evidence of particles of matter.

stem: The particles of matter are constantly:
solution: The particles of matter are continuously in motion; they possess kinetic energy, which increases with temperature, causing them to move faster.

stem: On increasing the temperature, the movement (kinetic energy) of the particles of matter:
solution: On heating, the particles of matter gain energy and move faster (their kinetic energy increases); this can cause changes of state, like melting or boiling.

stem: The change of a solid directly into a gas without becoming a liquid is called:
solution: Sublimation is the change of a solid directly into a gas (vapour) without passing through the liquid state — e.g. camphor, naphthalene balls and dry ice sublime.

stem: The change of a liquid into a gas (vapour) at any temperature from the surface is called:
solution: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour that occurs from the surface at any temperature (below the boiling point); it causes cooling.

stem: The change of a gas into a liquid on cooling is called:
solution: Condensation is the change of a gas (vapour) into a liquid on cooling — e.g. water vapour condensing into dew or the water droplets on a cold glass.

stem: When matter changes from one state to another (e.g. solid to liquid), it is a:
solution: A change of state (solid ↔ liquid ↔ gas) is a physical change — no new substance is formed, only the arrangement and energy of the particles change, and it is reversible.

stem: The spaces between particles are ______ in solids and ______ in gases.
solution: The spaces (gaps) between particles are very small in solids (tightly packed) and large in gases (particles far apart), with liquids in between.

stem: Solids have a definite shape and volume because their particles are:
options: Held tightly in fixed positions by strong forces
solution: Solids have a definite shape and volume because their tightly packed particles are held in fixed positions by strong intermolecular forces, so they cannot move freely.

stem: Gases can be compressed easily because:
options: There are large spaces between their particles
solution: Gases can be compressed easily because there are large spaces between their particles, which can be pushed closer together when pressure is applied.

stem: Which statement about the particulate nature of matter is correct? (i) Matter is made of tiny particles (ii) Particles are in constant motion (iii) There are spaces between particles
solution: All three are correct postulates of the particulate nature of matter: matter is made of tiny particles, the particles are in constant motion, and there are spaces between them.

stem: The rate of diffusion increases with:
solution: The rate of diffusion increases with increasing temperature, because the particles gain energy and move faster, mixing more quickly.

stem: A crystal of potassium permanganate placed in water spreads its colour throughout, showing:
options: Diffusion and the particulate nature of matter
solution: When potassium permanganate crystals are placed in water, their purple colour spreads throughout — showing that the tiny particles diffuse and mix with the water particles (particulate nature of matter).

stem: The reason we can walk through air but not through a wall is that:
options: The particles in a gas (air) are far apart, while in a solid (wall) they are tightly packed
solution: We can move through air because its particles are far apart with large gaps, but not through a wall because the particles in a solid are very tightly packed with strong forces holding them together.

stem: The state of matter in which particles have the highest kinetic energy is:
solution: Particles in the gaseous state have the highest kinetic energy — they move fastest and most freely — followed by liquids and then solids (lowest).

stem: The overall importance of understanding the particulate nature of matter is that it explains:
options: The properties of solids, liquids and gases, and processes like diffusion and changes of state
solution: The particulate nature of matter explains the properties and behaviour of solids, liquids and gases, and everyday processes like diffusion, dissolving, evaporation and changes of state.
